knowledge_point.title: Solving for Two Coefficients in a Linear Combination

question.:question/problem:
Consider the vectors

$$
{a}_{1}=\begin{bmatrix}3 \\ -3 \\ 1\end{bmatrix},\,{a}_{2}=\begin{bmatrix}-7 \\ 5 \\ -1\end{bmatrix},\,b=\begin{bmatrix}13 \\ -11 \\ 3\end{bmatrix}.
$$

If ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}=b,$ then what is ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}?$
question.:question/worked-solution:
If ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}=b$, then we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}\begin{bmatrix}3 \\ -3 \\ 1\end{bmatrix}+{x}_{2}\begin{bmatrix}-7 \\ 5 \\ -1\end{bmatrix} &=\begin{bmatrix}13 \\ -11 \\ 3\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}3{x}_{1} \\ -3{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{1}\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}-7{x}_{2} \\ 5{x}_{2} \\ -{x}_{2}\end{bmatrix} &=\begin{bmatrix}13 \\ -11 \\ 3\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}3{x}_{1}-7{x}_{2} \\ -3{x}_{1}+5{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{1}-{x}_{2}\end{bmatrix} &=\begin{bmatrix}13 \\ -11 \\ 3\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the corresponding components, we get the following system:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}3{x}_{1}-7{x}_{2} &=13 \\ -3{x}_{1}+5{x}_{2} &=-11 \\ {x}_{1}-{x}_{2} &=3\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Adding the first and the second equations we get

$$
\begin{aligned}-2{x}_{2} &=2 \\ {x}_{2} &=-1\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting ${x}_{2}=-1$ into the second equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}-3{x}_{1}+5{x}_{2} &=-11 \\ -3{x}_{1}+5(-1) &=-11 \\ -3{x}_{1} &=-6 \\ {x}_{1} &=2\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we substitute ${x}_{1}=2$ and ${x}_{2}=-1$ into the third equation to get

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}-{x}_{2} &=3 \\ (2)-(-1) &=3 \\ 3 &=3\end{aligned}
$$

which gives a true statement.

So the solution of the system is ${x}_{1}=2$ and ${x}_{2}=-1$, which means

$$
2{a}_{1}-{a}_{2}=b.
$$

Consequently,

$$
{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=(2)+(-1)=1.
$$

question.:question/problem:
Consider the vectors

$$
{c}_{1}=\begin{bmatrix}-1 \\ 3 \\ 5\end{bmatrix},\,{c}_{2}=\begin{bmatrix}4 \\ 1 \\ 2\end{bmatrix},\,d=\begin{bmatrix}-11 \\ -6 \\ -11\end{bmatrix}.
$$

If ${x}_{1}{c}_{1}+{x}_{2}{c}_{2}=d,$ then what is ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}?$
question.:question/worked-solution:
If ${x}_{1}{c}_{1}+{x}_{2}{c}_{2}=d$, then we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}\begin{bmatrix}-1 \\ 3 \\ 5\end{bmatrix}+{x}_{2}\begin{bmatrix}4 \\ 1 \\ 2\end{bmatrix} &=\begin{bmatrix}-11 \\ -6 \\ -11\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}-{x}_{1} \\ 3{x}_{1} \\ 5{x}_{1}\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}4{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2} \\ 2{x}_{2}\end{bmatrix} &=\begin{bmatrix}-11 \\ -6 \\ -11\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}-{x}_{1}+4{x}_{2} \\ 3{x}_{1}+{x}_{2} \\ 5{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2}\end{bmatrix} &=\begin{bmatrix}-11 \\ -6 \\ -11\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the corresponding components, we get the following system:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}-{x}_{1}+4{x}_{2} &=-11 \\ 3{x}_{1}+{x}_{2} &=-6 \\ 5{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2} &=-11\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Multiplying the first equation by $3$ and adding the result to the second equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}13{x}_{2} &=-39 \\ {x}_{2} &=-3\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting ${x}_{2}=-3$ into the first equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}-{x}_{1}+4{x}_{2} &=-11 \\ -{x}_{1}+4(-3) &=-11 \\ -{x}_{1} &=1 \\ {x}_{1} &=-1\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we substitute ${x}_{1}=-1$ and ${x}_{2}=-3$ into the third equation to get

$$
\begin{aligned}5{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2} &=-11 \\ 5(-1)+2(-3) &=-11 \\ -11 &=-11\end{aligned}
$$

which gives a true statement.

So the solution of the system is ${x}_{1}=-1$ and ${x}_{2}=-3$, which means

$$
-{c}_{1}-3{c}_{2}=d.
$$

Consequently,

$$
{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=(-1)+(-3)=-4.
$$

question.:question/problem:
Consider the vectors

$$
{a}_{1}=\begin{bmatrix}5 \\ 7 \\ -1\end{bmatrix},\,{a}_{2}=\begin{bmatrix}2 \\ 4 \\ 3\end{bmatrix},\,b=\begin{bmatrix}4 \\ -1 \\ -39/2\end{bmatrix}.
$$

If ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}=b,$ then what is ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}?$
question.:question/worked-solution:
If ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}=b$, then we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}\begin{bmatrix}5 \\ 7 \\ -1\end{bmatrix}+{x}_{2}\begin{bmatrix}2 \\ 4 \\ 3\end{bmatrix} &=\begin{bmatrix}4 \\ -1 \\ -39/2\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}5{x}_{1} \\ 7{x}_{1} \\ -{x}_{1}\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}2{x}_{2} \\ 4{x}_{2} \\ 3{x}_{2}\end{bmatrix} &=\begin{bmatrix}4 \\ -1 \\ -39/2\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}5{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2} \\ 7{x}_{1}+4{x}_{2} \\ -{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2}\end{bmatrix} &=\begin{bmatrix}4 \\ -1 \\ -39/2\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the corresponding components, we get the following system:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}5{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2} &=4 \\ 7{x}_{1}+4{x}_{2} &=-1 \\ -{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2} &=- \frac{39}{2}\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Multiplying the first equation by $-2$ and adding the result to the second equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}-3{x}_{1} &=-9 \\ {x}_{1} &=3\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting ${x}_{1}=3$ into the first equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}5{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2} &=4 \\ 5(3)+2{x}_{2} &=4 \\ 2{x}_{2} &=-11 \\ {x}_{2} &=- \frac{11}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we substitute ${x}_{1}=3$ and ${x}_{2}=- \frac{11}{2}$ into the third equation to get

$$
\begin{aligned}-{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2} &=- \frac{39}{2} \\ -(3)+3\left(- \frac{11}{2}\right) &=- \frac{39}{2} \\ - \frac{39}{2} &=- \frac{39}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

which gives a true statement.

So the solution of the system is ${x}_{1}=3$ and ${x}_{2}=- \frac{11}{2}$, which means

$$
3{a}_{1}-11/2{a}_{2}=b.
$$

Consequently,

$$
{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=(3)+\left(- \frac{11}{2}\right)=- \frac{5}{2}.
$$

question.:question/problem:
Consider the vectors

$$
{a}_{1}=\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ -1 \\ 2\end{bmatrix},\,{a}_{2}=\begin{bmatrix}-1 \\ -1 \\ 3\end{bmatrix},\,b=\begin{bmatrix}-9 \\ -7 \\ 23\end{bmatrix}.
$$

If ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}=b,$ then what is ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}?$
question.:question/worked-solution:
If ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}=b$, then we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ -1 \\ 2\end{bmatrix}+{x}_{2}\begin{bmatrix}-1 \\ -1 \\ 3\end{bmatrix} &=\begin{bmatrix}-9 \\ -7 \\ 23\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}{x}_{1} \\ -{x}_{1} \\ 2{x}_{1}\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}-{x}_{2} \\ -{x}_{2} \\ 3{x}_{2}\end{bmatrix} &=\begin{bmatrix}-9 \\ -7 \\ 23\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}{x}_{1}-{x}_{2} \\ -{x}_{1}-{x}_{2} \\ 2{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2}\end{bmatrix} &=\begin{bmatrix}-9 \\ -7 \\ 23\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the corresponding components, we get the following system:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}-{x}_{2} &=-9 \\ -{x}_{1}-{x}_{2} &=-7 \\ 2{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2} &=23\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Adding the first and the second equations we get

$$
\begin{aligned}-2{x}_{2} &=-16 \\ {x}_{2} &=8\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting ${x}_{2}=8$ into the first equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}-{x}_{2} &=-9 \\ {x}_{1}-(8) &=-9 \\ {x}_{1} &=-1 \\ {x}_{1} &=-1\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we substitute ${x}_{1}=-1$ and ${x}_{2}=8$ into the third equation to get

$$
\begin{aligned}2{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2} &=23 \\ 2(-1)+3(8) &=23 \\ 22 &=23\end{aligned}
$$

which gives a false statement.

So, the system has no solution.
